ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, point $D$ is on segment $BC$, $\angle EDB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$, $BE\perp DE$, and $DE$ intersects $AB$ at point $F$. If $BE=4$, what is the length of $DF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $DH\parallel AC$ through $D$ and meet $AB$ at $H$. Extend $BE$ to intersect with the extension of $DH$ at point $G$, as shown in the figure:\\
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle C=45^\circ$,\\
$\because DH\parallel AC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BDH=\angle C=45^\circ$, $\angle BHD=\angle A=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle HBD$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore HB=HD$,\\
$\because \angle EDB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle GDE=\angle EDB=22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore DE$ bisects $\angle BDG$,\\
$\because DE\perp BG$,\\
$\therefore \angle GED=\angle BED=90^\circ$,\\
In $\triangle BDE$ and $\triangle GDE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle GED=\angle BED=90^\circ \\
ED=ED \\
\angle GDE=\angle BDE=22.5^\circ
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BDE\cong \triangle GDE\left(AAS\right)$,\\
$\therefore BE=GE$, that is $BG=2BE$,\\
In $\triangle BGH$ and $\triangle DFH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle GBH=\angle FDH=22.5^\circ \\
BH=DH \\
\angle GHB=\angle FHD
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BGH\cong \triangle DFH(ASA)$,\\
$\therefore BG=DF$,\\
$\therefore DF=2BE=\boxed{8}$.

Now compare triangles BGH and DFH: H lies on AB and DG, F lies on AB and DE, ∠GHB=∠DHF=90°, BH=DH, and ∠GBH equals ∠FDH because each is the angle between a pair of perpendicular lines. 推理：由题设 AB=AC 且 ∠BAC=90°，可得 ∠ABC=∠ACB=45°。又 ∠EDB=1/2∠ACB=22.5°。
按指定方法，作 B 关于直线 DE 的对称点 G。因为 BE⊥DE 且 E 在 DE 上，所以 E 是 BG 的中点，BG=2BE=2×4=8。反射保持角度，D 在对称轴 DE 上，所以 ∠GDE=∠BDE=22.5°，于是 ∠BDG=22.5°+22.5°=45°。由于 AC 与 BC 成 45°，且 DG 与 DB 也成 45°，所以 DG∥AC。

因此 DF=BG=8。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, point $D$ is on segment $BC$, $\angle EDB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$, $BE\perp DE$, and $DE$ intersects $AB$ at point $F$. If $BE=4$, what is the length of $DF$?
raw_record.answer:
Construct $DH\parallel AC$ through $D$ and meet $AB$ at $H$. Extend $BE$ to intersect with the extension of $DH$ at point $G$, as shown in the figure:\\
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle C=45^\circ$,\\
$\because DH\parallel AC$,\\
$\therefore \angle BDH=\angle C=45^\circ$, $\angle BHD=\angle A=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle HBD$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore HB=HD$,\\
$\because \angle EDB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle GDE=\angle EDB=22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore DE$ bisects $\angle BDG$,\\
$\because DE\perp BG$,\\
$\therefore \angle GED=\angle BED=90^\circ$,\\
In $\triangle BDE$ and $\triangle GDE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle GED=\angle BED=90^\circ \\
ED=ED \\
\angle GDE=\angle BDE=22.5^\circ
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BDE\cong \triangle GDE\left(AAS\right)$,\\
$\therefore BE=GE$, that is $BG=2BE$,\\
In $\triangle BGH$ and $\triangle DFH$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle GBH=\angle FDH=22.5^\circ \\
BH=DH \\
\angle GHB=\angle FHD
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BGH\cong \triangle DFH(ASA)$,\\
$\therefore BG=DF$,\\
$\therefore DF=2BE=\boxed{8}$

Reflection preserves angles, and D is on the axis of symmetry DE, so ∠GDE=∠BDE=22.5°, hence ∠BDG=22.5°+22.5°=45°. Since AC forms 45° with BC, and DG also forms 45° with DB, DG∥AC.
Let H=AB∩DG. Because DG∥AC, and AB⊥AC, AB⊥DG, that is, ∠BHD=90°. Also ∠HBD=∠ABC=45°, so △BHD is an isosceles right triangle, BH=DH.
Compare △BGH and △DFH: H is on AB and DG, F is on AB and DE; ∠GHB=∠DHF=90°; BH=DH; and BG⊥DE, BH⊥DG, therefore ∠GBH equals ∠FDH, that is, both are corresponding angles formed by a set of mutually perpendicular straight lines. Therefore △BGH≅△DFH, obtaining DF=BG.
Therefore DF=BG=8.
